questions.question: What is cargo blocking?

options.text: It keeps cargo from moving during transport.
It can only be done with metal pieces.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps cargo from moving during transport.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing stop cargo from shifting while you are driving. Place blocks around the front, back, and sides of cargo to prevent it from moving.

questions.question: You are driving slowly through a construction zone and see a worker near the road. What should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down more.
questions.explanation: Always drive slowly in construction zones. Slow down even more if you see workers on or near the road.

questions.question: You see taillights ahead while driving in fog. What does this mean?

options.text: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the roadway.
You can be sure the vehicle is on the road.
It may be an optical illusion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the roadway.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable sign of where the road is. The lights you see may be from a vehicle that has left the road.

questions.question: How can you make your vehicle more visible during the day?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights for the best visibility, even during the day. High beam headlights can be dangerous around other drivers.

questions.question: When backing a truck, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is always risky because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both side mirrors often when backing. Use a helper whenever you can.

questions.question: Which crime will disqualify you from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.correctAnswerText: Arson
questions.explanation: A felony conviction for arson will prevent you from getting, renewing, or transferring a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), how should you brake?

options.text: Pump the brakes several times before holding the pedal down.
Press the brake pedal as hard as possible every time you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way in vehicles with ABS as in vehicles without ABS. ABS automatically works when you brake hard and prevents wheel lockup.

questions.question: How can you avoid slowing down traffic when driving a large truck?

options.text: Try to pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy truck cannot keep up with other traffic, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What does ABS allow you to do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control when stopping.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheel lockup during hard braking. Drive and brake the same way in vehicles with ABS as in vehicles without it.

questions.question: What is true about hydroplaning?

options.text: It can happen with very little water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with very little water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tire tread loses grip and your vehicle slides on water. You do not need much water for this to happen. Hydroplaning can start at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing during a driving test, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of your vehicle to check for a train.
Change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: How can a driver check if the road is becoming icy?

options.text: Try to guess if it is icy.
Open the window and touch the side mirror to feel for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the window and touch the side mirror to feel for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think the road may be icy but are not sure, open your window and feel the front of the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice has formed on these items, the road is likely becoming icy.

questions.question: What does rough acceleration do to your vehicle?

options.text: It is required on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause mechanical damage.
questions.explanation: Always speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine and parts.

questions.question: A 10-foot-long load must be secured with at least how many tie-downs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the size of the cargo.

questions.question: What should you pay extra attention to during a winter pre-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Coolant and antifreeze levels
questions.explanation: In winter, check the coolant level and antifreeze amount, heating and defrosting equipment, wiper blades, windshield washer, tires, tire chains, lights, reflectors, windows, mirrors, and exhaust system.

questions.question: How is alcohol removed from your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: By waiting.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The only way to sober up is to let your body remove the alcohol on its own over time.

questions.question: Why can parked delivery trucks be hazardous?

options.text: People may exit quickly without checking for other vehicles.
Packages often fall out and into the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: People may exit quickly without checking for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The driver may be in a hurry and pull into traffic without warning, or may suddenly step out without checking for other traffic.

questions.question: Which agency conducts the threat assessment for hazardous materials endorsements?
questions.correctAnswerText: The TSA
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts the threat assessment for applicants seeking a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: How can you increase your vehicle's visibility during dawn or dusk?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with your headlights on.
questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam to increase your vehicle's visibility.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle and you do not know how to put it out, what should you do?

options.text: Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: Do not try to put out a fire if you are unsure how. Move away from the flames and let firefighters handle it. This is especially important for hazardous materials fires.

questions.question: When drivers turn, they usually:

options.text: Look in the direction they are turning.
Look in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in the direction they are turning.
questions.explanation: When turning, drivers look in the direction they are turning. Even without using a turn signal, a driver's body movements may show they plan to turn.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is hard to see what is behind the vehicle.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see what is behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is always dangerous because the driver cannot see everything behind them. Drivers should avoid backing when possible.

questions.question: After a vehicle starts, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until you turn them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After a vehicle starts, warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections should be done:

options.text: Differently each time to check different items.
The same way each time so you don't forget anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This helps you learn all the steps and keeps you from missing anything.

questions.question: After an accident, use flares with caution because:

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see flares in sunny weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: After an accident, vehicle fires often happen when flares are used near spilled fuel. Use flares carefully.

questions.question: Your CDL will be revoked if:

options.text: You want to add an endorsement.
Your regular driving privilege is revoked.
You have not paid a toll.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your regular driving privilege is revoked.
questions.explanation: If your regular driving privilege is revoked, canceled, or suspended for moving traffic violations, you will lose your CDL. This does not apply to parking violations.

questions.question: When operating a truck that needs a CDL:

options.text: You never have to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if you carry more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if you drive a tank vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: The driver's seat must have a seat belt. You must wear a seat belt at all times when operating a truck.

questions.question: Which gas is a concern with a faulty exhaust system?
questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust system can let poisonous carbon monoxide enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not recommended on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: Any vehicle with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: When inspecting your vehicle, check for all of the following except:

options.text: Too much air pressure in your tires.
Too little air pressure in your tires.
The same tire brand name on all tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same tire brand name on all tires.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that air pressure in your tires is not too high or too low.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on the road.
questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is clear ice on the road. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice looks wet instead of icy. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet and the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: After stopping on the side of the road, you must within 10 minutes:
questions.correctAnswerText: Place emergency warning devices.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, you must place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes.

questions.question: Black ice is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Usually thin.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. The surface looks wet. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet and the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator is especially important:
questions.correctAnswerText: In cold weather.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: A person driving with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: A person who is dressed inappropriately.
A person who likes fresh air.

questions.correctAnswerText: A distracted driver.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs that a driver may be impaired. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are sleepy, use drugs, or are ill can be dangerous. One sign of an impaired driver is having windows rolled down in cold weather.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: Protecting the cargo from the weather
Preventing other drivers from looking at what is being transported

questions.correctAnswerText: Preventing other drivers from looking at what is being transported
questions.explanation: Cover cargo for two reasons: to protect people from spilled cargo and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: To avoid hitting a hazard on the road:

options.text: You should always try to stop.
Swerving may be safer than stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Swerving away from a hazard is sometimes safer than trying to stop. You can turn away from something faster than you can come to a complete stop.

questions.question: What happens to braking distance when you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph?
questions.correctAnswerText: It quadruples.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase braking distance. Doubling your speed from 20 to 40 mph increases braking distance by four times.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, leakage during a static test should not exceed ____ in one minute.
questions.correctAnswerText: 5 psi
questions.explanation: A static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should show no more than 5 psi loss in one minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repair and should not be driven.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection:

options.text: Should be done the same way every time.
Should be done differently every time.
Does not need to include all items every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you learn all steps and makes sure you do not forget to check anything.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. If the warning goes off while driving, stop the vehicle and get the system fixed.

questions.question: When traveling down a steep downgrade:

options.text: The air brakes should be used.
The vehicle should be placed in a low gear and the driver should use engine braking.
The driver should continually downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle should be placed in a low gear and the driver should use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep downhill roads, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only when needed to help slow down.

questions.question: When driving, being aware of what is happening behind you is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Important.
questions.explanation: You should know what is happening behind and to the sides of your vehicle. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder often.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks. It stops pumping when pressure gets too high and starts pumping when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts can mean they are loose.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts can mean the nuts are loose. If you see rust near the wheel nuts, check if they are tight before you drive.

questions.question: To warn drivers behind you that you will be slowing down, you should:

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal followed by the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to illuminate your brake lights.
Swerve from side to side to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to illuminate your brake lights.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This tells drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: If an unusual noise or feeling occurs in a vehicle while it is being driven, the driver should:

options.text: Assume it is not a concern and continue driving.
Hope the vehicle does alright until it is switched to another driver.
Check the situation to determine the proper solution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the situation to determine the proper solution.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel something wrong while driving, get it checked out.

questions.question: Mirrors should be:

options.text: Checked only if there is a reason to suspect a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked frequently.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving to watch for traffic and to check your own vehicle for problems.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system can:

options.text: Let poisonous fumes into the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let poisonous fumes into the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper area.
